Definition: to promise (pos., to do or give something to God)
BiblicalUsage: Nadar means to make a vow, to promise something to God, and the Bible treats a vow as a debt. In Genesis 28:20 Jacob vows that if God will be with him and keep him, the Lord shall be his God, and in Numbers 30:2 a man who vows a vow to the Lord shall not break his word. In Deuteronomy 23:21 he shall not slack to pay it, for the Lord will surely require it, and in Ecclesiastes 5:4 when you vow a vow to God, defer not to pay it, for He has no pleasure in fools.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a vow is a promise made to the one Person who never forgets, and that is why the Bible is so strict about it. Jacob vowed on the road and kept it, and the law says the keeping is the point. I hold that it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay.
